newsitem.title: USA: Helicopter crash kills Colgate-Palmolive executive.
newsitem.headline: Helicopter crash kills Colgate-Palmolive executive.

text.p: A helicopter crashed Tuesday afternoon into the East River in New York City, killing one man and injuring three, authorities said.

The accident involved a twin-engine helicopter belonging to Colgate-Palmolive Co.., the household products giant, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. On board were a pilot, a co-pilot and two passengers.
Police identified the dead passenger as Craig Tate, Colgate-Palmolive's chief technical officer. He died after being brought to nearby New York Hospital, hospital officials said.
Another Colgate executive, Jim Serafino, vice president and deputy general counsel, was listed in critical condition at New York Hospital, as was the helicopter's pilot, Ed Thurn.
The co-pilot, Rick Bird, was taken to Metropolitan Hospital, where he was listed in stable condition. Hospital authorities said he was conscious and conversant.

The Colgate executives were traveling from the company's research and development office in Piscataway, New Jersey. The company regularly uses a helicopter to shuttle employees from its New Jersey offices to its New York City headquarters, said company spokesman Bob Murray.
Police said the helicopter had just droppped off two passengers at the 60th Street heliport and was taking off again for White Plains, New York, when the accident occurred.

The crash was caused by the helicopter's rear rotor hitting the side of the heliport's administrative building, police said. It remained embedded in the wall of the structure as the helicopter fell upside-down into the river.
All four victims were pulled from the water, the Fire Department said.
Two emergency medical technicians who jumped in the river to rescue them were treated for exposure, authorities said.
The report of the crash, which occurred under clear sunny skies, came in at 5:36 p.m. EDT, the Fire Department said.
The National Transportation Safety Board and the FAA were working Tuesday night to haul the wreckage out of the river. The NTSB will investigate the cause of the crash, a FAA spokeswoman said.
Tate had been with the company for 30 years and was appointed CTO in 1994, He was in his 50s, and a resident of New Canaan, Connecticut, said a police spokesman.
